luke.17.p1.b2.text: It would be better for him to have a millstone hung around his neck and to be thrown into the sea than to cause one of these little ones to stumble.

luke.17.p1.b3.text: Watch yourselves. If your brother sins, rebuke him; and if he repents, forgive him.

luke.17.p1.b4.text: Even if he sins against you seven times in a day, and seven times returns to say, ‘I repent,’ you must forgive him.”

luke.17.p2.b2.text: “If you have faith the size of a mustard seed, you can say to this mulberry tree, ‘Be uprooted and planted in the sea,’ and it will obey you.

luke.17.p2.b3.text: Instead, won’t he tell him, ‘Prepare my meal and dress yourself to serve me while I eat and drink; and afterward you may eat and drink’?

luke.17.p2.b4.text: So you also, when you have done everything commanded of you, should say, ‘We are unworthy servants; we have only done our duty.’”

luke.17.p3.b1.text: While Jesus was on His way to Jerusalem, He was passing between Samaria and Galilee.

luke.17.p3.b2.text: As He entered one of the villages, He was met by ten lepers. They stood at a distance

luke.17.p4.b2.text: And as they were on their way, they were cleansed.

luke.17.p5.b1.text: When one of them saw that he was healed, he came back,

luke.17.p5.b2.text: praising God in a loud voice.

luke.17.p5.b3.text: He fell facedown at Jesus’ feet in thanksgiving to Him—and he was a Samaritan.

luke.17.p6.b1.text: “Were not all ten cleansed? … Where then are the other nine?

luke.17.p6.b2.text: Was no one found except this foreigner to return and give glory to God?”

luke.17.p6.b3.text: “Rise and go; your faith has made you well!”

luke.17.p7.b1.text: When the kingdom of God would come

luke.17.p7.b2.text: “The kingdom of God will not come with observable signs.

luke.17.p7.b3.text: Nor will people say, ‘Look, here it is,’ or ‘There it is.’

luke.17.p7.b4.text: For you see, the kingdom of God is in your midst.”

luke.17.p8.b1.text: “The time is coming when you will long to see one of the days of the Son of Man, but you will not see it.

luke.17.p8.b2.text: People will tell you, ‘Look, there He is!’ or ‘Look, here He is!’ Do not go out or chase after them.

luke.17.p8.b3.text: For just as the lightning flashes and lights up the sky from one end to the other, so will be the Son of Man in His day.

luke.17.p8.b4.text: But first He must suffer many things and be rejected by this generation.

luke.17.p9.b1.text: Just as it was in the days of Noah, so also will it be in the days of the Son of Man:

luke.17.p9.b2.text: People were eating and drinking, marrying and being given in marriage,

luke.17.p9.b3.text: up to the day Noah entered the ark. Then the flood came and destroyed them all.

luke.17.p10.b1.text: It was the same in the days of Lot: People were eating and drinking, buying and selling, planting and building.

luke.17.p10.b2.text: But on the day Lot left Sodom, fire and sulfur rained down from heaven and destroyed them all.

luke.17.p10.b3.text: It will be just like that on the day the Son of Man is revealed.

luke.17.p11.b1.text: On that day, let no one on the housetop come down to retrieve his possessions. Likewise, let no one in the field return for anything he has left behind.

luke.17.p11.b3.text: Whoever tries to save his life will lose it, but whoever loses his life will preserve it.

luke.17.p12.b1.text: I tell you, on that night two people will be in one bed: One will be taken and the other left.

luke.17.p12.b2.text: Two women will be grinding grain together: One will be taken and the other left.”

luke.17.p13.b2.text: “Wherever there is a carcass, there the vultures will gather.”
